measurement.happened:
THE SANCTIONS WAIVER AND DIESEL DEAL DOMINATES. The single biggest story of the week is that President Trump, just before a new sanctions law he himself signed was set to take effect, invoked 'national interest' to waive broad new Russia energy sanctions. He also struck a diesel deal with Moscow, under which Russia restarts diesel exports to the United States. Russia's Kremlin called the move 'historic.' Ukraine's Zelensky called it 'wrong' and a 'parody,' and US lawmakers from both parties pushed back hard, with at least one GOP member (Lawler) breaking with Trump over the diesel purchase. Germany's Merz warned that frozen Russian assets must stay in Europe, and the EU's Dombrovskis said 'now is not the time to ease Russian sanctions.' Meloni in Italy criticized the deal. The US also floated unfreezing some Russian assets to restart peace talks and weighed easing restrictions on the Russian and Iranian 'shadow fleet.' In short, the week was defined by Washington handing Moscow a diplomatic and economic gift at a moment when the war was intensifying, and Kyiv felt betrayed. Headlines from Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, and Al Jazeera all confirm this as the central narrative. (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, Al Jazeera – multiple headlines each.)

UKRAINE RESUMES STRIKES ON RUSSIAN REFINERIES; RUSSIA HITS ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE. After the 'energy ceasefire' that Trump had brokered fell apart, Zelensky declared 'we're done' and ordered Ukraine to resume missile and drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. A drone hit the Ryazan refinery, causing a fire. Ukraine also damaged six Russian military jets in a missile strike on an airfield, and drones hit an industrial site deep in western Siberia and the data center of Russia's largest bank. In response, Russia intensified its own campaign: it struck steel plants, power infrastructure, and ships across nine Ukrainian regions. At least eight civilians were killed in a single day, and over a million Ukrainians lost power. Russia said its attacks were aimed at forcing a blackout before winter. A new report showed a spike in civilian casualties. Ukraine said it was hurrying to build defenses against Russian jet-powered drones. Headlines from Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, and Al Jazeera all document this tit-for-tat escalation. (Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, Al Jazeera.)

RUSSIA BUILDS A NEW DRONE MEGABASE AND ESCALATES AIR POWER. Satellite images showed Russia had constructed a major new drone attack base in just six weeks. Strategic bombers made a planned flight over the Baltic Sea. Five Russian drones crashed on Moldovan territory, and Moldova condemned Moscow. Drone strikes in the Black Sea raised fears of a broader Russian escalation to test NATO's response. Romania accused Russia of attacking two tankers in NATO waters, and Bulgaria said Russia was likely behind Black Sea drone strikes as rescue operations continued. India urged both sides to protect Black Sea shipping. Latvia said a Baltic block of Russian grain might open a path to the Black Sea. Poland scrambled fighter jets as Russia struck western Ukraine. Headlines from Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, and Al Jazeera support this theme. (Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, Al Jazeera.)

DIPLOMATIC AND SUMMIT ACTIVITY. Zelensky attended an EU summit in Brussels where European leaders pledged continued support for Ukraine as the US backpedaled. He targeted both Trump and Putin at the summit. Zelensky also expressed hope for a trilateral meeting with the US and Russia at the upcoming G20 summit in Bangkok. Russia returned to the G20 table at the US invitation, which angered European leaders; Germany's Merz warned against bringing Russia back into the G20 fold, and at the IMF/World Bank meetings, delegates walked out on a Russian official. Pope Leo, recovering from lung cancer surgery, spoke by phone with Putin and asked for help for civilians in the besieged town of Oleshky; the Kremlin said Putin agreed to cooperate. Trump said he was in talks with Russia and China about denuclearization. A Putin envoy said Russia and the US were discussing joint deals including on data centers. Headlines from Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, and Al Jazeera cover this. (Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, Al Jazeera.)

ARRESTS, ESPIONAGE, AND INFORMATION WAR. Russia detained a Japanese journalist in the Far East on suspicion of spying; Tokyo protested and demanded explanations. Russia also arrested a Swedish man it said was planning 'terrorist acts' for Ukraine. A 26-year-old Russian officer defected to Ukraine and reportedly helped kill hundreds of Russian soldiers. Russia was found to be using an army of bots to push fake US election videos ahead of the midterms, and Russia, China, and Iran were all harnessing AI for US midterm disinformation. Novaya Gazeta's editor was questioned by Russian investigators over a colleague's case. Ukraine targeted Russia's equivalent of 'Google' as the internet became a new front line. The UK's MI5 chief warned of threats from Russia, Iran, and AI, and a Russian man linked to a deadly London hospitals hack was arrested. A fact-check debunked a misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity. Headlines from Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, and Al Jazeera support this. (Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, Al Jazeera.)

ECONOMIC AND ENERGY IMPACTS. Oil touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May, driven by Middle East tensions and fears over Russian supply. Russia's oil and gas revenue was seen up 10 percent year-on-year in October to about $12 billion. Russian fuel flows had fallen in early October before the diesel ban was eased. The global fuel oil market stayed tight as conflicts hit the Middle East and Russia's supplies. The Nord Stream trial continued, with the defense arguing Russia used the pipelines as a 'weapon.' Russia took over more EU companies' assets over Ukraine support. Rosatom targeted a year-end nuclear start-up at Turkey's Akkuyu plant and said a truce was in place for Zaporizhzhia power supply repairs. A magnitude-7 earthquake struck Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. Russian ministers joined the board of key trade payments firm A7. Headlines from Reuters, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, and Al Jazeera cover the economic dimension. (Reuters, DW, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, Al Jazeera.)

FRONTLINE AND TERRITORIAL DEVELOPMENTS. Ukraine said Russia's claimed territorial advances were 'an illusion,' and reported advancing in occupied Donetsk under Operation Vivaldi, with Starlink playing a key role. A Ukrainian foreign minister called a Russian-held town a 'death trap' with starving residents, and desperate civilians risked their lives along mined roads to escape. Putin said Russia was building a non-negotiable 'security zone' in Ukraine along the border. Restrictions exposed Ukraine's Starlink dependency. Headlines from Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, and Al Jazeera document the ground-level fighting. (Reuters, AP, BBC, DW, Al Jazeera.)
measurement.expected:
SANCTIONS AND DIESEL DEAL AFTERMATH – ALMOST CERTAIN. The political fight over Trump's sanctions waiver and diesel deal will continue to dominate. Expect congressional hearings, possible legal challenges over the legality of the waiver, and further public clashes between Zelensky and Trump. Russia will keep touting the deal as a victory. European leaders will press for a coordinated response. The question of whether the US will unfreeze some Russian assets to restart talks will be a live issue. Confidence: almost certain that this remains the top diplomatic story through the 24th.

CONTINUED AERIAL TIT-FOR-TAT – ALMOST CERTAIN. Ukraine will keep striking Russian refineries and industrial targets, and Russia will keep hitting Ukrainian energy infrastructure as winter approaches. Expect at least one more major Russian drone or missile wave on Ukraine and one or more Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries or airfields. Civilian casualties will remain elevated. The new Russian drone megabase will likely see its first operational use. Confidence: almost certain.

BLACK SEA AND BALTIC MARITIME TENSIONS – PROBABLE. With Romania, Bulgaria, and Poland all reporting incidents, expect at least one more drone or missile event near or over Black Sea or Baltic shipping lanes. NATO will be forced to respond diplomatically, and there is a real risk of a tanker being hit in NATO waters, which could push the alliance toward a more unified stance. India and other neutrals will keep calling for calm. Confidence: probable for at least one more incident; possible for a more serious escalation.

G20 AND MULTILATERAL DIPLOMACY – PROBABLE. The G20 summit in Bangkok is imminent. Zelensky has expressed hope for a trilateral meeting with the US and Russia. Expect Russia to use the G20 platform to project normalcy and to push its denuclearization agenda. European leaders will try to coordinate a message. The US-Russia data-center and joint-deal discussions will likely produce at least one announcement or working-level meeting. Confidence: probable that the G20 produces at least one Russia-related headline; possible that a trilateral or bilateral meeting is arranged.

ESPIONAGE AND INFORMATION WAR – PROBABLE. The Japanese journalist case will continue to generate diplomatic friction; Tokyo will press for either a release or a formal trial date. The Swedish arrest will be a smaller but persistent irritant. Russia's bot and AI disinformation campaigns aimed at the US midterms will intensify as the election date approaches. The UK will keep highlighting Russian hybrid threats, and the London hospitals hack case may produce a courtroom development. Confidence: probable that at least one of these threads produces a new headline.

NUCLEAR AND ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE – POSSIBLE. Rosatom's push to start up the Akkuyu unit by year-end will generate progress reports or delays. The Zaporizhzhia truce for repairs may either hold or break down, producing another crisis. Trump's denuclearization talks with Russia and China are early-stage and unlikely to produce a concrete deal this week, but expect at least one statement or working session. Confidence: possible for a nuclear-related headline; unlikely for a breakthrough.

DOMESTIC RUSSIA – POSSIBLE. The Kamchatka earthquake may produce follow-up on damage and rescue. The Novaya Gazeta investigation will continue. Russia's seizure of more EU company assets will be announced in batches. The A7 board appointment and other corporate moves will trickle out. Confidence: possible for one or two domestic items to make international news.

LESS LIKELY SURPRISES. A sudden Russian offensive on a new sector of the front (for example, a push toward the Dnieper or a flanking move in the south) that shifts the territorial picture. A second major Black Sea incident involving a NATO-flagged vessel that triggers a formal NATO Article 4 consultation. A Russian attempt to use the G20 to announce a unilateral 'peace package' that catches the West off guard. A follow-up earthquake or volcanic event in Kamchatka or the Kurils. A Russian cyber-attack on a Western energy or transport network that is publicly attributed.

THINGS I WOULD NOT BET ON. A full or partial ceasefire being announced this week. Russia accepting a formal territorial concession or a 'security zone' being defined in a written agreement. The Japanese journalist being released before a formal charge is filed. A major Russian mobilization announcement or a new round of conscription. A Russian nuclear test or a new ICBM launch that is publicly confirmed. A Russian domestic political crisis (for example, a ministerial reshuffle or a regional governor sacking) that makes international headlines. A second magnitude-7-plus earthquake in the same week.
emoji_reasons: Trump's last-minute waiver of new Russia sanctions and the diesel deal were the single most consequential and most widely covered event of the week, reshaping the US-Ukraine-Russia dynamic overnight.

Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian refineries while Russia intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, and a new Russian drone megabase was revealed, making the aerial war the most visible battlefield development.

Zelensky's EU summit, the G20 return of Russia, the Pope-Putin phone call, and the US-Russia data-center and denuclearization talks all show that diplomacy, for all its frustrations, remained the other major axis of the week.
